assessment.text: The premise holds on this record without strain: two consecutive quarterly filings put Data Center growth on a year earlier at 92% and then 117%, so the segment is not only growing but growing faster.

The fiscal-year basis tells a different story from the quarterly one: annual Data Center growth slowed by 74.2 percentage points, while quarterly revenue growth has since sped up by 20.6 percentage points, so the slowdown belongs to the older annual comparison and the newest quarters point the other way.

What the claim does not carry is the step to the decision: holding overweight into the next report needs the growth to continue past the newest 10-Q, and the record's only forward-looking item is the filing's own warning that faster product transitions may make revenue volatile.

The quality of the growth carries a caution, since receivables grew faster than revenue and receivable days rose to 59.6 from 54.1, a result the corollary marks as running against what the claim implies.

Receivables growing +126.8% against revenue's +105.9% means a growing part of reported sales is not yet cash, and the record has no deferred revenue to show whether orders back the next quarter.

Leadership turnover has run through the year, from the chief accounting officer and the head of worldwide field operations to the CEO himself, and the record cannot say whether it touches sales execution.

The shares are shifting rather than settling: the largest single customer went from 22% for fiscal 2026 to 21% in Q1 FY2027, and the first-half figures top out at 16%, which points to a buyer set that is rotating or broadening, not to one buyer growing more dominant.

The step from concentration to the overweight decision is the real question, and the record does not back it in either direction: concentration is a fragility, but in this record it sits beside revenue that more than doubled and growth that sped up by 20.6 percentage points, nearly all of it from Data Center.

The one place concentration might show up in the numbers is collection: receivables grew faster than revenue and receivable days rose to 59.6 from 54.1, but the record does not say which customers hold those balances.

analysis.corollary_rule: A corollary is an implication a model proposed and code computed. Each is read by the grammar and by the typed form the proposing model wrote: two readers, which is weaker than the two-of-three rule the thesis's own claims are read under. A corollary never moves a verdict; when most of a claim's computed corollaries come out against it, the claim is flagged.
analysis.audit_rule: A sentence is verified by code when every id it cites is in this run, at least one is evidence, and every number it writes is carried by that evidence: a verified finding's quotes and cited figures, an analytic's value, inputs and reading, a computed test's operands and result, a reported figure, an 8-K event's text. The claim's own words carry no number, and neither does the sentence a model wrote for a corollary: only what code computed for it does. A threshold is a third thing: when a number equals the threshold of a computed test or corollary the sentence cites, or a condition's own threshold, the sentence is not failed for it, and it is listed as a threshold restated, not checked as a fact. A bare year is carried by a cited item dated in that year. The audit does not decide whether a sentence follows from what it cites.
analysis.persistence_method: Resampling with replacement: 10,000 paths of 4 quarters, each step drawn from the measure's own last N quarterly changes (differences in points for a percent, growth rates for an amount), from the current value; the share of paths in which the test holds in every one of the 4 quarters. Seed 20261118. It assumes the past changes are exchangeable: it ignores trend, seasonality and anything not in the facts. It describes the history; it is not a forecast.

weakest_why.text: The year-over-year margin test passes with room of only 1.27x a typical move, and it held in just 12 of 20 past readings, so the expansion reading is fragile on its own history.
The comparison base is depressed by the prior year's $4.5 billion H20 charge. On a full-year basis the claim fails, by -3.9 points, which makes the expansion a recovery rather than a new gain.
Sequentially the gain is +0.04 points, which the filing itself describes as approximately flat, so nothing in the record backs margin as a source of upside into the report.

strongest_for.text: Revenue rose in each of the last 8 quarters, at a compound +15.7% a quarter. Year-over-year growth also sped up by 20.6 percentage points in the newest quarter, so the trend into the report is accelerating rather than fading.
Data Center is outgrowing the company and its share rose to 92.5% from 87.9%, so the line the thesis depends on is gaining weight, not losing it.
Customer concentration is not visibly intensifying. Q2 FY2027 names one direct customer at 16%, against three in Q1 at 21%, 17% and 16%, which softens the concentration risk.

strongest_against.text: The CEO's immediate resignation, with the CFO as interim CEO, is an execution risk landing squarely in the holding period, and the record has no evidence to size it.
Receivables grew +126.8% against revenue growth of +105.9%, a result that runs against what the growth claim implies. It raises the question of how much of the growth has turned into cash.

On the annual basis, Data Center growth slowed by 74.2 percentage points, and the filing warns that faster product transitions may make revenue volatile. With one segment at 92.5% of revenue, any stumble in it hits the whole company.

bottom_line.text: The thesis's central premise holds and is strengthening: Data Center growth on a year earlier rose to +116.6%. The segment supplied +102.5 percentage points of the +105.9% total growth, so the overweight case rests almost entirely on one line of business.

The margin leg adds little to that case. Gross margin is 0.2 percentage points below where it was eight quarters ago, and the filing calls it approximately flat sequentially, so any earnings upside into the report has to come from revenue rather than margin.

The risk claims are true as disclosures, but none yet shows in the numbers. The one computable China test runs against the export-control claim by +97.7 points, and the company's own concentration and supplier warnings sit beside a quarter of unbroken growth.

The record ends before the decision's horizon. The CEO resigned effective immediately in an 8-K filed after the newest 10-Q, and none of the financial evidence can weigh what that means for the next report.
The quality of the growth carries two cautions the bullish claims do not address. Receivable days rose to 59.6 from 54.1, and inventory days rose to 119.3 from 105.6.
A careful investor would want three things from the next filing: whether quarterly revenue stays above $96.22B, whether receivable days stop climbing, and how the leadership transition is disclosed.
